exercises.heading: 15.9. Exercises

problem.paragraph: Match the given transformation with the image (labeled I, II, III, IV, V and VI) of the set $$S = \left\{ {\left( {u,\upsilon} \right)|0 \leqslant u \leqslant 1,0 \leqslant \upsilon \leqslant 1} \right\}$$ under the transformation. Give reasons for your choices.

exercises.instruction: 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 Find the image of the set $$S$$ under the given transformation.

problem.paragraph: $$S = \left\{ {\left( {u,\upsilon} \right)|0 \leqslant u \leqslant 1,0 \leqslant \upsilon \leqslant 2} \right\}$$ ; $$x = u + \upsilon$$ , $$y = - \upsilon$$
$$S = \left\{ {\left( {u,\upsilon} \right)|0 \leqslant u \leqslant 3,0 \leqslant \upsilon \leqslant 2} \right\}$$ ; $$x = 2u + 3\upsilon$$ , $$y = u - \upsilon$$
$$S$$ is the square bounded by the lines $$u = 0$$ , $$u = 1$$ , $$\upsilon = 0$$ , $$\upsilon = 1$$ ; $$x = \upsilon$$ , $$y = u{({1 + \upsilon^{2}})}$$
$$S$$ is the triangular region with vertices $$\left( {0,0} \right)$$ , $$\left( {1,1} \right)$$ , $$\left( {0,1} \right)$$ ; $$x = u^{2}$$ , $$y = \upsilon$$

solution.paragraph: The region bounded by the line $$y = 1$$ , the $$y$$ -axis, and $$y = \sqrt{x}$$

problem.paragraph: $$S$$ is the disk given by $$u^{2} + \upsilon^{2} \leqslant 1$$ ; $$x = au$$ , $$y = b\upsilon$$

exercises.instruction: 7, 8, 9, and 10 A region $$R$$ in the $$\mathit{xy}$$ -plane is given. Find equations for a transformation $$T$$ that maps a rectangular region $$S$$ in the $$u\upsilon$$ -plane onto $$R$$ , where the sides of $$S$$ are parallel to the $$u$$ - and $$\upsilon$$ -axes.

solution.paragraph: $$x = \frac{1}{3}\left( {\upsilon - u} \right)$$ , $$y = \frac{1}{3}\left( {u + 2\upsilon} \right)$$ is one possible transformation, where $$S = \left\{ {\left( {u,\upsilon} \right)| - 1 \leqslant u \leqslant 1,1 \leqslant \upsilon \leqslant 3} \right\}$$

problem.paragraph: $$R$$ is the parallelogram with vertices $$\left( {0,0} \right)$$ , $$\left( {4,3} \right)$$ , $$\left( {2,4} \right)$$ , $$\left( {- 2,1} \right)$$
$$R$$ lies between the circles $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 1$$ and $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 2$$ in the first quadrant

solution.paragraph: $$x = u\cos\upsilon$$ , $$y = u\sin\upsilon$$ is one possible transformation, where $$S = \left\{ {\left( {u,\upsilon} \right)|1 \leqslant u \leqslant \sqrt{2},0 \leqslant \upsilon \leqslant \pi \slash 2} \right\}$$

problem.paragraph: $$R$$ is bounded by the hyperbolas $$y = 1 \slash x$$ , $$y = 4 \slash x$$ and the lines $$y = x$$ , $$y = 4x$$ in the first quadrant

exercises.instruction: 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, and 22 Use the given transformation to evaluate the integral.

problem.paragraph: $$\iint_{R}{\left( {x - 3y} \right)\mathit{dA}}$$ , where $$R$$ is the triangular region with vertices $$\left( {0,0} \right)$$ , $$\left( {2,1} \right)$$ , and $$\left( {1,2} \right)$$ ; $$x = 2u + \upsilon$$ , $$y = u + 2\upsilon$$

$$\iint_{R}{\left( {4x + 8y} \right)\mathit{dA}}$$ , where $$R$$ is the parallelogram with vertices $$\left( {- 1,3} \right)$$ , $$\left( {1, - 3} \right)$$ , $$\left( {3, - 1} \right)$$ , and $$\left( {1,5} \right)$$ ; $$x = \frac{1}{4}\left( {u + \upsilon} \right)$$ , $$y = \frac{1}{4}\left( {\upsilon - 3u} \right)$$
$$\iint_{R}{x^{2}\mathit{dA}}$$ , where $$R$$ is the region bounded by the ellipse $$9x^{2} + 4y^{2} = 36$$ ; $$x = 2u$$ , $$y = 3v$$

$$\iint_{R}{{({x^{2} - xy + y^{2}})}\mathit{dA}}$$ , where $$R$$ is the region bounded by the ellipse $$x^{2} - xy + y^{2} = 2$$ ; $$x = \sqrt{2}u - \sqrt{2 \slash 3}\upsilon$$ , $$y = \sqrt{2}u + \sqrt{2 \slash 3}\upsilon$$

$$\iint_{R}{xy\mathit{dA}}$$ , where $$R$$ is the region in the first quadrant bounded by the lines $$y = x$$ and $$y = 3x$$ and the hyperbolas $$xy = 1$$ , $$xy = 3$$ ; $$x = u \slash \upsilon$$ , $$y = \upsilon$$

$$\iint_{R}{y^{2}\mathit{dA}}$$ , where $$R$$ is the region bounded by the curves $$xy = 1$$ , $$xy = 2$$ , $$xy^{2} = 1$$ , $$xy^{2} = 2$$ ; $$u = xy$$ , $$\upsilon = xy^{2}$$ . Illustrate by using a graphing calculator or computer to draw $$R$$ .

list.item: Evaluate $$\iiint_{E}\mathit{dV}$$ , where $$E$$ is the solid enclosed by the ellipsoid $$x^{2} \slash a^{2} + y^{2} \slash b^{2} + z^{2} \slash c^{ 2} = 1$$ . Use the transformation $$x = au$$ , $$y = b\upsilon$$ , $$z = cw$$ .

The earth is not a perfect sphere; rotation has resulted in flattening at the poles. So the shape can be approximated by an ellipsoid with $$a = b = 6378{km}$$ and $$c = 6356{km}$$ . Use part (a) to estimate the volume of the earth.
If the solid of part (a) has constant density $$k$$ , find its moment of inertia about the $$z$$ -axis.

problem.paragraph: An important problem in thermodynamics is to find the work done by an ideal Carnot engine. A cycle consists of alternating expansion and compression of gas in a piston. The work done by the engine is equal to the area of the region $$R$$ enclosed by two isothermal curves $$xy = a$$ , $$xy = b$$ and two adiabatic curves $$xy^{1.4} = c$$ , $$xy^{1.4} = d$$ , where $$0 < a < b$$ and $$0 < c < d$$ . Compute the work done by determining the area of $$R$$ .

exercises.instruction: 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, and 30 Evaluate the integral by making an appropriate change of variables.

problem.paragraph: $$\iint\limits_{R}{\frac{x - 2y}{3x - y}\mathit{dA}}$$ , where $$R$$ is the parallelogram enclosed by the lines $$x - 2y = 0$$ , $$x - 2y = 4$$ , $$3x - y = 1$$ , and $$3x - y = 8$$
$$\iint_{R}{\left( {x + y} \right)e^{x^{2} - y^{2}}\mathit{dA}}$$ , where $$R$$ is the rectangle enclosed by the lines $$x - y = 0$$ , $$x - y = 2$$ , $$x + y = 0$$ , and $$x + y = 3$$

$$\iint\limits_{R}{\cos\left( \frac{y - x}{y + x} \right)\mathit{dA}}$$ , where $$R$$ is the trapezoidal region with vertices $$\left( {1,0} \right)$$ , $$\left( {2,0} \right)$$ , $$\left( {0,2} \right)$$ , and $$\left( {0,1} \right)$$
$$\iint_{R}{\sin{({9x^{2} + 4y^{2}})}\mathit{dA}}$$ , where $$R$$ is the region in the first quadrant bounded by the ellipse $$9x^{2} + 4y^{2} = 1$$
$$\iint_{R}{e^{ x + y}\mathit{dA}}$$ , where $$R$$ is given by the inequality $${|x|} + {|y|} \leqslant 1$$
$$\iint\limits_{R}{\frac{y}{x}\mathit{dA}}$$ , where $$R$$ is the region enclosed by the lines $$x + y = 1$$ , $$x + y = 3$$ , $$y = 2x$$ , and $$y = x/2$$

Let $$f$$ be continuous on $$\left\lbrack {0,1} \right\rbrack$$ and let $$R$$ be the triangular region with vertices $$\left( {0,0} \right)$$ , $$\left( {1,0} \right)$$ , and $$\left( {0,1} \right)$$ . Show that
$$\iint\limits_{R}{f\left( {x + y} \right)\mathit{dA} = {\int_{0}^{1}{uf(u)\mathit{du}}}}$$
